label: USE CASE 09
title: How an AI Coding Assistant Builds a Feature

scenes.text: Let's watch an AI coding assistant take a real request, add a dark mode button to a website, [1] and follow every step it takes, from reading code to shipping. [2] Here's how an AI builds a feature.

title: AI Builds
A Feature
data.subtitle: Step by step, like a real developer

scenes.text: Here's the whole journey. [1] You ask, add a dark mode toggle to my website. [2] The agent explores the repo, and finds the header and style files. [3] It writes a plan, add a button, add dark colours, and remember the choice. [4] It edits three files, [5] and runs the app and the tests, to check that everything works.

Let's zoom in on its first move. [1] You ask for the dark mode toggle. [2] The agent calls a tool, search files, for the header and theme colours. [3] It finds three relevant files. [4] And it replies with a plan, before touching any code.

data.heading: First move: explore
data.question: Add a dark mode toggle to my website.
data.answer: Found the header and theme files. My plan: add a toggle, add dark colours, and save your choice.

scenes.text: Then it does the work, like a careful developer. [1] It adds a toggle button to the header. [2] It adds a set of dark colours to the styles. [3] And it saves your choice, so the site remembers it next time.

data.heading: Doing the work
steps: A dark theme in the styles

scenes.text: Then comes testing, the most important part. [1] It loops, test, read the error, and fix. [2] The first test run fails, because the button text is invisible in dark mode. [3] It reads the error, and fixes the text colour. [4] It runs the tests again, [5] and now everything passes.

log: error: button text invisible in dark mode
fix: set the text colour for dark mode

scenes.text: And before it ships, a few good practices. [1] Show the diff, so a human sees every change. [2] Small commits, one clear change at a time. [3] Human review, where someone approves it. [4] And a pull request, the formal way to propose changes to a project.

Here's a common myth. [1] People think the AI just writes the code once, perfectly. [2] Real coding agents make mistakes too. What makes them useful is the loop, running tests, reading errors and fixing them, plus a human reviewing the result.

data.myth: The AI writes the code once, perfectly.
data.fact: Agents make mistakes too. The test-and-fix loop plus human review is what makes them useful.
